Ayy one of my favorite series of all time. Bless you Nihom Falcom. Now, fangirling aside - I really liked my time with Celceta even though I do have some reservations with this game. Keep in mind, however - Ys: Memories of Celceta is a port of the original PSVita title, which is a remake of 2, yes 2 Ys games. Keeping that in mind, the game has some pacing issues towards the middle part of the game. 

Obviously, this being a port of a Vita title, the visuals are serviceable if not a little rough around the edges, but it works. The game is very pretty in motion, there's a fairly robust beastiary and the characters look great in combat. Environments are a little bare bones and basic, but serviceable. 

Gameplay is always the bread and butter of Ys games and this one isn't much different. The combat is simplistic and this game in particular is one of the easier Ys games - but it's overall great. You have your normal attacks and Skills, skills use a shared pool between your current party called EXTRA, you can chain them together, combo into them, etc, it definitely makes the gameplay feel much more fluid when used in combos and most characters have a wide variety of skills that do very different things from each other! You also have 2 defensive skills, you have a Guard and a dodge roll (that's a lil busted); if you time your guard perfectly, you get what's called a Flash Guard, which will dramatically increase your critical hit rate and nullify damage - on the opposite end, if you dodge attacks last second, you get a "witch time" esque mechanic that slows down time and lets you wail on your opponent while nullifying damage - the most broken aspect about it, is you could often Flash Guard then dodge at the end of the animation for both slow time AND critical rate up, which made a LOT of fights very trivial. 

There's a couple sidequests you can do as you get to new towns, which are kinda basic and uninspired, the better parts of these were for world building but otherwise don't really offer much but extra gold that does help. The game follows a bit of a formulaic pacing at the start, you get maybe 3 sets of weapons/armors till the midway point, which is when the game just goes at a breakneck pace all the way to the ending. There's also crafting systems to make accessories which was largely unneeded unless you wanted extras of ones you had for other characters, there's a refining system that lets you buff weapons and armors but you more than likely won't use it whatsoever until you get the best in slot weapons at the very end, but you will use the Gemstones you DO get to buff up your weapons with status effects (which are kinda broken lol - abuse Freeze).

The story is pretty basic JRPG, and even more basic for Ys titles. You are Adol Christin and you have now lost your memories, you save some folks in a mine then are entrusted with mapping out the Great Forest, which really turns into it's own story down the line as you meet new characters. You, of course, end up on a quest to save the world and whatnot, this is Ys, you already know what to expect. 

Score is great as always as well, bless you Falcom Sound Team but that voice acting, it's both barely existant, since most story is told with text but when characters DO talk, it's very stiff. Sound effects are also just OK, but not much expected there since it IS a Vita port. All in all though, I greatly enjoyed my time with the game despite the wonky pace of the game past the halfway point. If you're new to the Ys series, I do NOT recommend starting out with this game however, the game is very simplistic and you could get a bit more out of playing other entries - if you're just looking for a fun romp through a forest with a bit of a melodramatic story and fun characters or are already a fan of Ys/Xanadu, definitely worth the pickup!

..........*sigh*......It really hurts me to do this. I have loved Falcom since the mid 2000's when I first played Ys 6, and ever since then I've gone through as much of their library as possible. The Ys series has always had a special place in my heart and I never thought the series could fail me. Well......I stand corrected.

To clarify, I am very much biased to Falcom in the 2000's AKA Trails in the Sky, Ys 6, Oath, Origin, etc. So for me, Ys 7 was already a step down, but at least the structure of the game was still fun. Here, I have to be honest, the idea of roaming around in the forest to peice Adol's memories together is so damn boring. It's so focused on being open-ended and not about having a fun path towards the next dungeon/town/whatever. This structure does not help the game at all since the battle system is in my opinion, crap.

This game continues the party system from Ys 7 with skills, charge attacks, etc. I think this system pales in comparison to something like Oath or Origin. It no longer focuses on speed, movement, and magic use, and instead focuses on blocking, dodging, skills, and switching party members. The act of adding in more mechanics ironically makes the game more shallow as athe game now has to cope with all these different ways to fight instead of being laser focused with tertiary mechanics like magic to freshen up combat later on.

The story and characters are also just uninteresting at best, and cringey at worst. It's not all that bad since the story in Ys games aren't entirely important, but at least the characters usually have some intrigue to them in the other games. Not a terrible point, but still worth mentioning.

Now, it does say I don't recommend this game, but don't take that to mean this game is awful. Steam's binary system annoys me so in order for me to truly rate this compared to all the other Ys games then I have to downvote it. There are just too many other great Ys games for me not to. It's not awful, but its mediocrity is what kills it for me. This might be the first Falcom game I have no interest in finishing.

[b]Memories of Celceta[/b] and [url=store.steampowered.com/app/587100]Ys SEVEN[/url] act as this awkward mid-point between the Ark engine trilogy ([url=store.steampowered.com/app/312540]The Ark of Napishtim[/url], [url=store.steampowered.com/app/207320]The Oath in Felghana[/url] and [url=store.steampowered.com/app/207350]Origin[/url]) and modern Ys ([url=store.steampowered.com/app/579180]Lacrimosa of Dana[/url] and [url=store.steampowered.com/app/1351630]Monstrum Nox[/url]). If you're new to the series, I'd suggest playing Lacrimosa of Dana, The Oath in Felghana and Origin first, as they're considered the crème de la crème of the series (and the stories are largely self-contained so the order doesn't matter). Memories of Celceta is a mildly enjoyable game but pales in comparison to these legends.

If you want the short of it, Memories of Celceta is basically Lacrimosa of Dana but worse, with the few key points being:
- No camera control. And the fixed camera here is not the cool zoomed out isometric camera like in the Ark engine games but this awkward zoomed in low angle one, more like in the old Devil May Cry games.
- There's no jump button, and this means no platforming challenges or any aerial moves or attacks. As a result, the dungeon design is largely uninspired and the combat is one note.
- It uses the same party system as Lacrimosa of Dana but each party member has a unique ability (e.g. only Duren can pick locks and only Ozma can break cracked walls), so even if you don't care for a particular party member you still need to swap them in and out all the time.
- Very little content, the game has a lot of padding and copy pasted areas but the playtime is still only 20-25 hours compared to 50+ in Lacrimosa of Dana.

This game is technically a remake of Ys IV, but there were actually two Ys IV games ([b]Mask of the Sun[/b] and [b]The Dawn of Ys[/b]), both released in 1993 and outsourced to different studios. Memories of Celceta is a Falcom made canon remake that combines both stories (with mixed results). The game opens with Adol stumbling out of the Great Forest of Celceta having lost all of his memories. Your job is to go back and find out what actually happened. You enlist some help along the way, starting with Duren (who's literally not-Dogi with a different hair style because real Dogi would break the amnesia plot device) and a few more anime tropes whose character arcs end the moment they join the party.

The narrative is largely poor as it relies too heavily on the amnesia gimmick and the ending is very abrupt and very reminiscent of a certain popular fantasy movie trilogy. The general writing tone doesn't help much as the majority of the dialog is characters stating the obvious or wasting your time by repeating the same things over and over again. There are a lot of cutscenes and a lot of talking but very little of it is meaningful. Still, there are some nice moments, like the roo village or some lore nods to The Ark of Napishtim.

The mechanics have an illusion of complexity but offer little depth in practice and every boss plays the same. Spam normal attacks to charge your SP bar, then spam skills to charge your EXTRA bar, when the boss is stunned use the EXTRA skill for epic damage. You don't even need to dodge, just spam the Flash Guard button when the boss telegraphs something. You only need to time the first parry, after that you can just keep spamming Flash Guard for literal god mode [i]while you're still inside the attack hitbox[/i]. But that's on the higher difficulties, on Normal and below you can just facetank and heal.

Just like in Lacrimosa of Dana there's material gathering and crafting but it's largely useless. I only ever bothered crafting some accessories, weapon enhancing is not worth the grind as you're getting a new weapon tier after practically every boss, so it's a waste of time to invest into any single weapon.

The graphics are okay for a Vita game, the awful HDR/bloom can be [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2345585622]turned off[/url] and the game looks pretty good without it, on par with [url=store.steampowered.com/app/538680]Trails of Cold Steel[/url] 1/2.

Now let me be more specific why

The bad
[list]
 [*]protagonist has a very serious case amnesia(which also has extremely silly explanation down the line) to the point he doesn't remember anything, even his childhood years.

[*]main cast of characters you get into your party is bland and their stories are uninteresting

Really more of a thumb sideways, but ultimately there was a bit more here that disappointed me than stuff I enjoyed.

The combat is reasonably good. It didn't blow me away, but it does what it's supposed to and mostly I had fun with it. The story is pretty underwhelming. What really tips this to a thumbs down for me, though, is the exploration. There's just not a whole lot there - you run over a bunch of fields and uncover areas under fog of war, and that's kind of it. Compared both to reference points like various Legend of Zelda games, and to newer titles in the Ys series, it doesn't feel like there's a whole lot there. Memories has a real problem with forgetting the new traversal tools you get as soon as you leave the dungeon you got them in. At best there are some underwater chests that you can spend a kind of unreasonable amount of time backtracking to for some pretty okay accessories once you get the swimming artifact.

If you're a massive Ys junkie, you've already played half the series and you're craving more, you probably don't need me to tell you that you'll like this game too. If you're not, though, I can't really recommend this compared to a lot of other games in the same vein.

Also I kind of want the concept of UI design to physically manifest just to punch whoever decided that your "character-specific interact with objects on the field to solve puzzles" button and your EXTRA skill button (your limit break, basically) should be the *same* button square in the junk. You can at least decouple the binds in the menu, but it sure is a jump scare the first time you waste an entire gauge of important combat resource when you're a quarter inch off where the game thinks you should be to pick a lock or see a memory.
